title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.

providers.name: GitHub Enterprise Cloud
providers.scope_notes: Enterprise Cloud feature scope. Fine-grained PATs, classic PATs and GitHub Apps have different approval/revocation rules.

controls.name: Restrict personal access tokens (classic) from accessing your organizations
controls.what: Blocks classic PATs from org-owned resources; public resources stay reachable.
controls.setting: Org settings > Personal access tokens > Settings > Tokens (classic) tab
controls.quote: Restrict access via personal access tokens: Personal access tokens (classic) or fine-grained personal access tokens cannot access resources owned by the organization. SSH keys created by personal access tokens will continue to work.

controls.name: Restrict access via personal access tokens (enterprise policy)
controls.what: Enterprise owners block classic and/or fine-grained PATs from all enterprise orgs; orgs cannot override.
controls.setting: Enterprise settings > Policies > Personal access tokens
controls.quote: Restrict access via personal access tokens: Personal access tokens cannot access organizations owned by the enterprise. SSH keys created by these personal access tokens will continue to work. Organizations cannot override this setting.

controls.name: Set maximum lifetimes for personal access tokens
controls.what: Blocks member PATs whose lifetime exceeds the limit from org resources; tokens are not revoked. Enterprise can set a ceiling.
controls.setting: Org settings > Personal access tokens > Settings (per token type); Enterprise settings > Policies > Personal access tokens
controls.quote: For fine-grained personal access tokens, the default the maximum lifetime policy for organizations is set to expire within 366 days. Personal access tokens (classic) do not have an expiration requirement.

controls.name: Require SAML SSO authentication for all members
controls.what: Members must authenticate via the IdP; classic PATs and SSH keys must be SSO-authorized, and OAuth/GitHub App user authorizations need an active SSO session.
controls.setting: Org settings > Authentication security > SAML single sign-on; or enterprise-level SAML
controls.quote: You must authorize your personal access token (classic) after creation before the token can access an organization that uses SAML single sign-on (SSO).

controls.name: Revoke SSO authorizations / Delete keys and tokens
controls.what: Owners revoke SSO authorizations (SAML) or delete credentials (EMU only) per user, per credential type, or in bulk.
controls.setting: Org settings > Authentication security; enterprise incident response; REST API
controls.plan: GitHub Enterprise Cloud (SAML SSO or EMU)
controls.quote: Revoking authorizations removes SSO authorizations for user tokens and SSH keys, either for a specific user, all users, or a specific credential type, across all organizations in your enterprise.

controls.name: IP allow list
controls.what: Blocks PATs, OAuth app tokens, SSH/deploy keys, GitHub App tokens and GITHUB_TOKEN from non-allowed IPs (not user-installed apps' installation tokens).
controls.setting: Org settings > Authentication security > IP allow list; Enterprise settings > Authentication security
controls.quote: IP allow lists don't currently restrict access when a GitHub App is installed on a user account and uses server-to-server installation tokens to access an organization or enterprise.

no_control.what: Classic PATs cannot be put under an approval workflow; only fine-grained PATs can.
no_control.quote: Only fine-grained personal access tokens, not personal access tokens (classic), are subject to approval.

controls_unknown: Whether admins can set a maximum lifetime for GitHub App user access tokens or OAuth app tokens (only app-developer settings found).
Whether GITHUB_TOKEN workflow permission defaults can be made non-overridable.

authentication.summary: Classic/fine-grained PATs, OAuth app tokens, GitHub App installation/user tokens, and Actions GITHUB_TOKEN.

federation.details: This path uses a local/static or platform-native credential. Evaluate a separate federation path where listed.

ip_restriction.boundary: Allowlist covers authenticated web/API/Git. Exceptions exist, including installation tokens for apps installed on a personal user account.

lifetime.summary: User-chosen expiry or none; classic PATs have no expiration requirement unless an enterprise/org owner sets a maximum lifetime. Revoked if unused for one year.

renewal.summary: No refresh token. An expired or revoked PAT cannot be restored; the owner creates a new token. PATs unused for one year are revoked automatically.

administration.summary: Repository/permission-scoped apps and PATs; PAT approval/restriction and lifetime policy; SAML authorization; revoke tokens or suspend/uninstall apps.
administration.conditions: Enterprise Cloud feature scope. Fine-grained PATs, classic PATs and GitHub Apps have different approval/revocation rules.

sso.details: With SAML/OIDC SSO, a classic PAT must be SSO-authorized for the org before it can reach org resources; with EMU OIDC, IdP CAP IP conditions are checked on each PAT authentication.

offboard.details: Offboarded users' PATs can no longer access enterprise/org resources; EMU hard-deprovisioning deletes them.

inventory.details: Enterprise Settings > Authentication security > Credentials 'Export CSV' lists classic_pat credentials enterprise-wide (enterprise owners; org owners have no direct visibility).

sso.ui: Org Settings > Authentication security > Require SAML SSO authentication (or Enterprise Settings > Authentication security > Require SAML authentication); user authorizes token via Developer settings > Personal access tokens > Configure SSO; admin reviews under People > member > SAML identity linked > Authorized credentials

usage.ui: Enterprise Settings > Audit log; search hashed_token:"<base64 SHA-256>" (hash from token or credential inventory CSV)

reads.ui: Enterprise Settings > Audit log > Export Git Events > pick date range > Download Results; filter JSON on action git.clone and hashed_token

offboard.ui: Org > People > select member > Remove from organization; Enterprise > People > ... > Remove from enterprise; EMU: deprovision in IdP (SCIM)

token_format.notes: Prefix documented; GitHub publishes no regex/length. Secret scanning type github_personal_access_token.

log_sources.name: GitHub organization/enterprise audit log
log_sources.notes: Records token-authenticated actions with hashed_token, programmatic_access_type, token_scopes. 180 days; Git events 7 days and only via REST include=git, streaming or export. IP disclosure is opt-in.

log_sources.name: GitHub user security log
log_sources.notes: Token owner's own log: PAT/OAuth create, update, destroy events. Owner-visible only.

log_sources.name: Audit log streaming (enterprise)
log_sources.notes: Needed to keep Git events beyond 7 days; api.request events (enterprise setting, streaming only).

log_sources.name: Enterprise credential inventory export
log_sources.notes: CSV with hashed_token, credential_id and SSH key fingerprint to match against audit events.

log_sources.name: Secret scanning alerts
log_sources.notes: secret_scanning_alert.* events; GitHub auto-revokes tokens pushed to public repos/gists.

Common field; mapping to REST ids not documented
Scopes of the token, if any

lifecycle_events.notes: Member authorized the PAT for SAML/OIDC SSO in the org
Docs: may appear when a PAT expires or is revoked (security log)

anomaly_cues: hashed_token seen from new country/ASN or user_agent unlike the owner's tooling
burst of git.clone across many repos by one hashed_token
classic PAT use after owner left org or after SSO revoke attempt
token_scopes include admin:org, delete_repo or workflow on a token used only for read
use shortly after secret_scanning_alert.create or public_leak

containment.steps: Owner deletes token in settings; anyone with the value can POST it to the credential revocation API; org/enterprise owners revoke its SSO authorization or restrict classic PAT access by policy; EMU owners can delete credentials.
containment.notes: Deleting/revoking ends the token. SSO revoke only blocks SSO-protected orgs; token still works elsewhere. Org owners cannot list classic PATs.

sample_query.purpose: All web/API events by one leaked classic PAT (hash with: echo -n TOKEN | openssl dgst -sha256 -binary | base64); add include=git via REST for Git events.
